name: glow_mod
description: A small fictional Fabric mod (examples/glow_mod): Java code, a data pack (functions, recipe, loot table), assets (item models, en_us / tr_tr translations), a YAML config copied out of the jar, a client payload, a game test, a byte-identical copy of one function under datapack/, and a reference tree (reference/original-plugin, the Paper plugin it was ported from) declared as index.reference. 14 questions, 7 Turkish and 7 English: callers x3, cross_layer x2, config x2, resources x2, flow, behaviour x2, where x2 (one of them explicitly about the original plugin).
verified_by: Gold facts were written by reading every file of examples/glow_mod line by line; every source.at line was re-read by hand after the example was finished, and each fact's source.at/source.contains pair is re-checked against the benchmark copy before any approach is scored (metrics.validate_gold).

provenance.questions_written_by: an agent asked by the Verinoda maintainer to write examples/glow_mod and this set in one session; it did not run Verinoda on the example and saw no Verinoda output for these questions
provenance.gold_written_by: same agent, by reading every file of examples/glow_mod; checked with metrics.validate_gold only
provenance.example_written_by: same agent, same session, before the questions
provenance.caveat: held out for Verinoda's retrieval on these questions (no Verinoda run and no Verinoda output while writing them), but not independent of the design: the Minecraft support (resource ids, data-pack linking, reference trees, class-qualified Java calls, Turkish passive caller questions) was developed against a similar private mod by the same project, and this example was written afterwards by an agent that knew which of those features it should exercise

facts.fact: GlowCommands.wisp (/glow wisp) calls Wisp.spawn at the command source's position (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/command/GlowCommands.java:29)
the UseBlockCallback registered by LanternEvents.etkinlestir calls Wisp.spawn above a soul lantern (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/event/LanternEvents.java:30)
Ritual.baslat calls Wisp.spawn once per ritual wisp around the altar (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/ritual/Ritual.java:29)
WispSpawner.onChunkLoad (ServerChunkEvents.CHUNK_LOAD hook) calls Wisp.spawn on a swamp surface (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/world/WispSpawner.java:31)
ServerNetworking.onSummonWisp (server handler of SummonWispPayload) calls Wisp.spawn (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/network/ServerNetworking.java:29)
the game test WispTests.wispAppearsWhereAsked calls Wisp.spawn (src/gametest/java/com/example/glowmod/test/WispTests.java:16)

negatives.statement: Wisp.onDeath calls Wisp.spawn (a dying wisp runs the wisp_death function; it spawns no new wisp)
client code calls Wisp.spawn directly (the client only sends SummonWispPayload)

facts.fact: GlowMod.onInitialize calls GlowConfig.load first, at mod start (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/GlowMod.java:21)
GlowCommands.reload (/glow reload) calls GlowConfig.load again (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/command/GlowCommands.java:45)

negatives.statement: the code that reads settings (RepairScheduler, Ritual, WispSpawner, ServerNetworking) calls GlowConfig.load (it only calls GlowConfig.get)

questions.question: Bir wisp öldüğünde hangi eşyalar düşüyor ve bunlar nerede tanımlanıyor?
questions.question_en: When a wisp dies, which items drop and where is that defined?

facts.fact: Wisp.onDeath runs the data-pack function by its bare name: Datapack.run(serverWorld, getPos(), "wisp_death") (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/entity/Wisp.java:42)
Datapack.run prepends the mod namespace, so "wisp_death" is glowmod:wisp_death = data/glowmod/function/wisp_death.mcfunction (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/util/Datapack.java:16-18)

wisp_death.mcfunction summons a glowmod:wisp_heart item named "Wisp Heart" at the death spot (src/main/resources/data/glowmod/function/wisp_death.mcfunction:4; identical copy datapack/data/glowmod/function/wisp_death.mcfunction:4)
the wisp's entity loot table drops 0-2 glowmod:ember_shard (src/main/resources/data/glowmod/loot_table/entities/wisp.json:9-13)

negatives.statement: Wisp.onDeath calls Datapack.runQualified (it passes the bare name to Datapack.run)

questions.question: Which Java code runs the glowmod:ritual/start data pack function?

facts.fact: Ritual.baslat runs it by its full id: Datapack.runQualified(..., "glowmod:ritual/start") (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/ritual/Ritual.java:22)
Datapack.runQualified parses the full id with Identifier.of(id) (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/util/Datapack.java:21-23)
Datapack.execute looks the function up and runs it through the server's command function manager at the altar position (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/util/Datapack.java:25-35)
the /glow ritual command reaches it: GlowCommands.ritual calls Ritual.baslat (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/command/GlowCommands.java:40)

negatives.statement: Ritual.baslat calls Datapack.run (it calls Datapack.runQualified with the full id)

questions.question: glowmod:ritual/tick fonksiyonu nereden çağrılıyor?
questions.question_en: Where is the glowmod:ritual/tick function called from?

facts.fact: ritual/start.mcfunction calls it once with `function glowmod:ritual/tick` (src/main/resources/data/glowmod/function/ritual/start.mcfunction:7)
ritual/tick.mcfunction reschedules itself every tick while an altar marker exists (src/main/resources/data/glowmod/function/ritual/tick.mcfunction:5)
indirectly from Java: Ritual.baslat runs glowmod:ritual/start (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/ritual/Ritual.java:22)

negatives.statement: Ritual.baslat runs glowmod:ritual/tick directly (it runs ritual/start, which calls ritual/tick)

questions.question: Where is glowmod.yml loaded and where do its default values come from?

facts.fact: GlowConfig.load reads glowmod.yml from the Fabric config directory (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/config/GlowConfig.java:26-42)
when the file does not exist yet, the default is copied out of the mod jar (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/config/GlowConfig.java:29-33)
the bundled default file is src/main/resources/glowmod.yml (src/main/resources/glowmod.yml:1-18)

source.contains: Copied to config/glowmod.yml on first start

facts.fact: missing keys and an unreadable file fall back to DEFAULTS = new GlowConfig(4, 0.02, 8, 40, 8) (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/config/GlowConfig.java:18)
it is loaded at mod start by GlowMod.onInitialize (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/GlowMod.java:21)

negatives.statement: GlowConfig reads config.yml (that file belongs to the original plugin under reference/)

questions.question: Her tick'te kaç bloğun onarılacağı nerede ayarlanıyor?
questions.question_en: Where is it set how many blocks are repaired per tick?

facts.fact: repair.blocks_per_tick: 8 in the default config (src/main/resources/glowmod.yml:11-12)
GlowConfig.parse reads repair.blocks_per_tick, default 8 (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/config/GlowConfig.java:51)
RepairScheduler.tick uses it as the per-tick repair budget (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/repair/RepairScheduler.java:33-39)

negatives.statement: the mod reads the hyphenated key blocks-per-tick (that is the original plugin's config.yml)

questions.question: Where is the crafting recipe for the lantern staff and what goes into it?

facts.fact: a shaped crafting recipe in src/main/resources/data/glowmod/recipe/lantern_staff.json whose result is glowmod:lantern_staff (src/main/resources/data/glowmod/recipe/lantern_staff.json:14-17)
ingredients: E = glowmod:ember_shard, L = minecraft:soul_lantern, S = minecraft:stick (src/main/resources/data/glowmod/recipe/lantern_staff.json:9-13)
pattern " EL" / " SE" / "S  ": two ember shards, one soul lantern, two sticks (src/main/resources/data/glowmod/recipe/lantern_staff.json:4-8)

questions.question: Fener asasının (lantern_staff) eşya modeli ve oyunda görünen adı hangi dosyalarda tanımlı?
questions.question_en: In which files are the lantern staff's item model and in-game name defined?

facts.fact: item model src/main/resources/assets/glowmod/models/item/lantern_staff.json (parent minecraft:item/handheld, texture glowmod:item/lantern_staff)
English name: "item.glowmod.lantern_staff": "Lantern Staff" (src/main/resources/assets/glowmod/lang/en_us.json:2)
Turkish name: "item.glowmod.lantern_staff": "Fener Asası" (src/main/resources/assets/glowmod/lang/tr_tr.json:2)
the item itself is registered as glowmod:lantern_staff in ModItems (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/item/ModItems.java:13)

questions.question: How does pressing the summon key on the client end up spawning a wisp on the server?

facts.fact: GlowModClient registers the key binding key.glowmod.summon_wisp (G) (src/client/java/com/example/glowmod/client/GlowModClient.java:19-23)
on a key press while looking at a block, onEndTick sends SummonWispPayload(hit.getBlockPos()) (src/client/java/com/example/glowmod/client/GlowModClient.java:28)
SummonWispPayload is a record with id glowmod:summon_wisp carrying a BlockPos (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/network/SummonWispPayload.java:11-15)
ServerNetworking.register registers the C2S payload type and onSummonWisp as its receiver (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/network/ServerNetworking.java:15-18)

onSummonWisp requires the lantern staff in the main hand and a distance within max_summon_distance, then calls Wisp.spawn above the block (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/network/ServerNetworking.java:20-30)

negatives.statement: the server handler sends the payload (direction reversed)

questions.question: Sunucu kapanırken henüz onarılmamış bloklara ne oluyor?
questions.question_en: What happens to blocks that are not repaired yet when the server shuts down?

facts.fact: RepairScheduler.register hooks temizle to ServerLifecycleEvents.SERVER_STOPPING (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/repair/RepairScheduler.java:25)
temizle puts every pending block back at once, without the per-tick budget or the delay (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/repair/RepairScheduler.java:42-45)
then the queue is emptied (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/repair/RepairScheduler.java:46)

negatives.statement: the per-tick repair handler calls temizle

questions.question: Where are the mod's items registered?

facts.fact: ModItems.register puts each item into Registries.ITEM under glowmod:<name> (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/item/ModItems.java:20-22)
the items are the fields LANTERN_STAFF, EMBER_SHARD and WISP_HEART (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/item/ModItems.java:13-15)
GlowMod.onInitialize calls ModItems.initialize, which loads the class and adds the items to creative tabs (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/GlowMod.java:22)

questions.question: Oyuncu fener asasıyla bir ruh fenerine sağ tıklayınca ne oluyor?
questions.question_en: What happens when a player right-clicks a soul lantern with the lantern staff?

facts.fact: the UseBlockCallback from LanternEvents.etkinlestir reacts only server-side, to the lantern staff in hand on a soul lantern (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/event/LanternEvents.java:19-26)
a wisp is spawned in the block above the lantern (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/event/LanternEvents.java:30)
the staff then gets a 100-tick cooldown; during it the click fails (src/main/java/com/example/glowmod/event/LanternEvents.java:12, 27-31)

negatives.statement: using the staff on a lantern starts the ritual

questions.question: In the original Paper plugin, how was a wisp spawned and what called it?

facts.fact: the plugin's Wisp.spawn spawns an Allay named "Wisp" and tags it with a persistent wisp key (reference/original-plugin/src/main/java/com/example/glowplugin/Wisp.java:19-24)
WispListener.onInteract calls it when a soul lantern is right-clicked with a blaze rod (reference/original-plugin/src/main/java/com/example/glowplugin/WispListener.java:19-27)
